chapter.title: You Can Acquire the Habit of Happiness

concepts.title: Happiness as pleasant mental activity
concepts.content: The chapter adopts Schindler’s description of happiness as having pleasant thoughts much of the time. The author uses a practical mental-habit definition to shift the discussion from reward and entitlement to attention and experience.

concepts.title: Mental-state medical claims require boundaries
concepts.content: The text draws a broad connection between cheerful thinking and health, citing anecdotes and older medical assertions. Emotional state and physiology are presented as tightly linked, often extending well beyond what is actually demonstrated.

concepts.title: Prosocial attention and nontransactional happiness
concepts.content: Helping others is portrayed as a potential source of satisfaction rather than a tax on a fixed happiness supply. Shifting attention toward another person’s needs may foster meaning and appreciation; it need not require self-sacrifice.

author_practices.title: Thirty-day shoe-order and daily-intention experiment
author_practices.content: Book structure: Notice which shoe is normally put on first and usual lace-tying motion. For the next 30 days choose the reverse order or another safe small change as a daily reminder. Use the reminder to attempt the 8 listed intentions: cheerfulness, friendliness, tolerance, acting toward a goal, fact/opinion separation, smiling three times, measured calm response, and letting go of unchangeable pessimistic claims. At the end observe any real-life changes without treating the timeline as universal. Timing: 30 days; each morning shoe cue; 3 smiles during each day among other daily intentions
